observation_summary: NumberUtils.createNumber incorrectly assumes all 8-digit hex strings fit into an Integer, failing to account for signed integer overflow when the leading digit is 8 or greater.
hypothesis: The NumberUtils.createNumber method incorrectly classifies hex strings as Integers if they have 8 digits, even if the value exceeds Integer.MAX_VALUE (e.g., 0x80000000). The current logic only checks the length of the hex string without considering the magnitude of the leading digit, causing an overflow when Integer.decode() is called.
prediction: The code in NumberUtils.createNumber will fail to correctly identify that 0x80000000 requires a Long, and will instead pass it to createInteger, which uses Integer.decode() and throws a NumberFormatException because 0x80000000 is outside the range of a signed 32-bit integer.
experiment_rationale: The bug report and stack trace confirm that 0x80000000 causes a NumberFormatException in createInteger. The logic in createNumber (lines 466-474) uses a simple length check (hexDigits > 8) to decide between Integer and Long, which is insufficient for signed hex values.
reasoning_summary: The defect is a missing validation check on the magnitude of the hex number (specifically the leading digit) before deciding whether to treat it as an Integer or a Long. This is a classic boundary condition error in predicate logic.

alternative_types.why_not_primary: The core issue is the decision logic (the predicate) used to select the target type, not the implementation of the conversion algorithm itself.
